This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed\n\n\fIntroduction\nE*HealthLine.com, Inc ’s EHI Export feature allows privileged users in Inpatient and ambulatory settings to efficiently\nexport a single patient's EHI data in multiple formats. This capability streamlines the extraction of clinical and healthcare\ndata, including demographics, billing information, encounters, notes, and more.\nThis document will inform users on how to perform the export features in EHR and describe the file structure and formats\nof the extracted files\n\n170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information Export\nE*HealthLine.com, Inc Export Batch CCDA option is accessible from Data Maintenance Menu; meets the following\nrequirements\n(i)(A)(B)(D)(E) Single Patient Electronic Health Information Export:\nThe health IT developer attests that a user of the Health IT Module can perform an electronic health information (EHI)\nexport for a single patient at any time the user chooses without developer assistance and that the export file(s):\n• Is created in a timely fashion;\n• Includes all the EHI for a single patient as described in § 170.315(b)(10)(i)(A);\n• Is electronic and in a computable format; and\n• Includes a publicly accessible hyperlink of the export’s format.\n(i)(C) Single Patient Electronic Health Information Export:\nThe health IT developer attests that the Health IT Module can limit users who can perform an EHI export for a single\npatient using one of the following methods:\n• Grant a set of users the ability to perform the export; or\n• Grant system administrator(s) the ability to perform the export.\nPatient Population Electronic Health Information Export:\nThe health IT developer attests that a user of the Health IT Module can perform an EHI export for all electronic health\ninformation, and that the export:\n• Includes all the EHI for a patient population as described in § 170.315(b)(10)(ii);\n• Is electronic and in a computable format; and\n• Includes a publicly accessible hyperlink of the export’s format.\nDocumentation:\nThe health IT developer attests that the health IT developer has a process for keeping the export format(s) used to\nsupport paragraphs (b)(10)(i) and (ii) of this section up-to-date.\n\n170.315(g)(10) ‐ Standardized API For Patient and Population services\nConfidential\nPage 4 of 10\n©2023 E*HealthLine.com All rights reserved. This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed\n\n\fEXPORT FORMAT:\nSingle patient and patient population EHI is exported in the following format\n\nFile Structure andDescription\nThe downloaded file is packaged in a .zip folder. The content of the zip file includes the patient's EHI data such as\nallergies, encounters, lab results, procedures, billing information, images etc. Below is an example of the extracted files\nand folders:\n•\n\nDocuments – this is a CDA XML DOC Export file containing the “Documents” folder containing patient’s supporting\ndocuments or attachments when available.\n\n•\n\nNotes - this is a CDA XML DOC Export file folder containing all the notes recorded during the patient’s previous\nmedical visits/encounters.\n\n•\n\nBillingReport - this is a CSV file containing the patients financial transactions with their provider. The information\nincludes the patient information, transaction dates, charges, claims and the description of transactions made with status.\n\n•\n\nCCDA - is an XML file export of a patient's clinical data. The system allows exports of HL7 CCDA which complies\nwith United States Core Data for Interoperability (USCDI), Version 1 requirements. The specifications for the CCDA\ncan be obtained from the HL7 website.\n\n•\n\ndemographics - this is a CSV file that contains the patient's key information, identification details, contact information,\ninsurance information etc.\n\n•\n\nPatientDocumentFiles - this is a CSV mapping file that contains the list of patients documents. This file outlines the\ncontents of the patients supporting attachments contained in the “Documents” folder.\n\n•\n\nSchedule - a CSV file, that contains a record of the patient’s encounters with specific information including\nappointment date, provider, location, appointment type, workflow, notes and date on which notes are recorded.\n\n170.315(g)(10) ‐ Standardized API For Patient and Population services\nConfidential\nPage 5 of 10\n©2023 E*HealthLine.com All rights reserved. This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed\n\n\fMulti-Patient Data Export\nE*HealthLine.com, Inc has the capability to export all data for a patient population, delivering the exported data in a .zip\nfolder following the same format as described below. To obtain the data,\n\nFile Structure andDescription\nThe downloaded file is packaged in a .zip folder. The content of the zip file includes the patient's EHI data such as\nallergies, encounters, lab results, procedures, billing information, images etc. Below is an example of the extracted\nfiles and folders:\n•\n\nDocuments – this is a CDA XML DOC Export file containing the “Documents” folder containing patient’s supporting\ndocuments or attachments when available.\n\n•\n\nNotes - this is a CDA XML DOC Export file folder containing all the notes recorded during the patient’s previous\nmedical visits/encounters.\n\n•\n\nBillingReport - this is a CSV file containing the patients financial transactions with their provider. The information\nincludes the patient information, transaction dates, charges, claims and the description of transactions made with status.\n\n•\n\nCCDA - is an XML file export of a patient's clinical data. The system allows exports of HL7 CCDA which complies\nwith United States Core Data for Interoperability (USCDI), Version 1 requirements. The specifications for the CCDA\ncan be obtained from the HL7 website.\n\n•\n\ndemographics - this is a CSV file that contains the patient's key information, identification details, contact information,\ninsurance information etc.\n\n•\n\nPatientDocumentFiles - this is a CSV mapping file that contains the list of patients documents. This file outlines the\ncontents of the patients supporting attachments contained in the “Documents” folder.\n\n•\n\nSchedule - a CSV file, that contains a record of the patient’s encounters with specific information including\nappointment date, provider, location, appointment type, workflow, notes and date on which notes are recorded.\n\n170.315(g)(10) ‐ Standardized API For Patient and Population services\nConfidential\nPage 6 of 10\n©2023 E*HealthLine.com All rights reserved. This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed\n\n\fExport Batch CDA – Update\nThe CDA Export Screen has been updated to comply with 170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information Export criteria.\nAll documents from CDA Batch export screen will now be exported in a CCDA format New options include;\n\n−\n−\n−\n−\n\n<Clinic Logon>- For selecting a specific clinic to export from\n<Include Chart Document >- exports CDA and includes Chart Documents\n<Show Sticky Note on TIF docs> - Option to include Sticky Notes on TIF documents when choosing the\n<Include Chart Documents> Option\nOption to include or exclude Custom Patient Data Tables in the CDA\n\nThe rest of the functionality remains the same; please see the full Export Batch CCDA documentation for additional\ninformation\nThe following features comply with 170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information Export criteria:\n\nLimit users who can perform an EHI export\nThis functionality is not new, but applies to 170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information Export criteria; the logged-on\nuser must have the following privileges granted by the E*HEALTHLINE.COM, INC Admin user.\nTo grant privileges;\n\n1. Log in as the E*HealthLine.Com, Inc Admin user, edit <Security Roles> for the selected user\n2. In the Security Roles Settings screen select the [Edit General Database Setup] privilege and check one (or\nboth) of the following privileges; [Print Documents] or [Chart Reviewer]\n3. Save Changes, Close\n4. To remove this EHI Export access privilege, uncheck the <Edit General Database Setup> option OR\nuncheck the <Print Documents> and <Chart Reviewer> options\n\n170.315(g)(10) ‐ Standardized API For Patient and Population services\nConfidential\nPage 7 of 10\n©2023 E*HealthLine.com All rights reserved. This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed\n\n\fIntroduction\nE*HealthLine.com, Inc ’s EHI Export feature allows privileged users in Inpatient and ambulatory settings to efficiently\nexport a single patient's EHI data in multiple formats. This capability streamlines the extraction of clinical and healthcare\ndata, including demographics, billing information, encounters, notes, and more.\nThis document will inform users on how to perform the export features in EHR and describe the file structure and formats\nof the extracted files\n\n170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information Export\nE*HealthLine.com, Inc Export Batch CCDA option is accessible from Data Maintenance Menu; meets the following\nrequirements\n(i)(A)(B)(D)(E) Single Patient Electronic Health Information Export:\nThe health IT developer attests that a user of the Health IT Module can perform an electronic health information (EHI)\nexport for a single patient at any time the user chooses without developer assistance and that the export file(s):\n• Is created in a timely fashion;\n• Includes all the EHI for a single patient as described in § 170.315(b)(10)(i)(A);\n• Is electronic and in a computable format; and\n• Includes a publicly accessible hyperlink of the export’s format.\n(i)(C) Single Patient Electronic Health Information Export:\nThe health IT developer attests that the Health IT Module can limit users who can perform an EHI export for a single\npatient using one of the following methods:\n• Grant a set of users the ability to perform the export; or\n• Grant system administrator(s) the ability to perform the export.\nPatient Population Electronic Health Information Export:\nThe health IT developer attests that a user of the Health IT Module can perform an EHI export for all electronic health\ninformation, and that the export:\n• Includes all the EHI for a patient population as described in § 170.315(b)(10)(ii);\n• Is electronic and in a computable format; and\n• Includes a publicly accessible hyperlink of the export’s format.\nDocumentation:\nThe health IT developer attests that the health IT developer has a process for keeping the export format(s) used to\nsupport paragraphs (b)(10)(i) and (ii) of this section up-to-date.\n\n170.315(g)(10) ‐ Standardized API For Patient and Population services\nConfidential\nPage 4 of 10\n©2023 E*HealthLine.com All rights reserved. This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed\n\n\fEXPORT FORMAT:\nSingle patient and patient population EHI is exported in the following format\n\nFile Structure andDescription\nThe downloaded file is packaged in a .zip folder. The content of the zip file includes the patient's EHI data such as\nallergies, encounters, lab results, procedures, billing information, images etc. Below is an example of the extracted files\nand folders:\n•\n\nDocuments – this is a CDA XML DOC Export file containing the “Documents” folder containing patient’s supporting\ndocuments or attachments when available.\n\n•\n\nNotes - this is a CDA XML DOC Export file folder containing all the notes recorded during the patient’s previous\nmedical visits/encounters.\n\n•\n\nBillingReport - this is a CSV file containing the patients financial transactions with their provider. The information\nincludes the patient information, transaction dates, charges, claims and the description of transactions made with status.\n\n•\n\nCCDA - is an XML file export of a patient's clinical data. The system allows exports of HL7 CCDA which complies\nwith United States Core Data for Interoperability (USCDI), Version 1 requirements. The specifications for the CCDA\ncan be obtained from the HL7 website.\n\n•\n\ndemographics - this is a CSV file that contains the patient's key information, identification details, contact information,\ninsurance information etc.\n\n•\n\nPatientDocumentFiles - this is a CSV mapping file that contains the list of patients documents. This file outlines the\ncontents of the patients supporting attachments contained in the “Documents” folder.\n\n•\n\nSchedule - a CSV file, that contains a record of the patient’s encounters with specific information including\nappointment date, provider, location, appointment type, workflow, notes and date on which notes are recorded.\n\n170.315(g)(10) ‐ Standardized API For Patient and Population services\nConfidential\nPage 5 of 10\n©2023 E*HealthLine.com All rights reserved. This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed\n\n\fMulti-Patient Data Export\nE*HealthLine.com, Inc has the capability to export all data for a patient population, delivering the exported data in a .zip\nfolder following the same format as described below.
